question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 5 & -1 \\ 4 & 0 & 10 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 & 5 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix given above. Identify **all** of the reasons why one can conclude that $|A|=0?$

I. $A$ has identical columns

II. $A$ has a zero column

III. $A$ has identical rows
question.worked_solution:
Let's examine each of the statements in turn.

- $A$ does *not* have identical columns.

- $A$ has a zero column: 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 5 & -1 \\ 4 & 0 & 10 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 & 5 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\,✓
$$

- $A$ has identical rows: 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 5 & -1 \\ 4 & 0 & 10 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 & 5 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\,✓
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
